decisions.reason: As a differentiated low-noise extension of the established infrared-heating line, it likely remains acceptable under current aspirations and is not costly enough to force immediate withdrawal in a growing market.
Because it had its own product page and fits the firm's core offer closely, management would likely view it as meeting aspirations well enough to retain.
This radiant-heater variant appears less prominently and may underperform relative to internal aspirations and comparable firms, making it a plausible target for portfolio pruning.

A tube-heater model still fits the firm's established competence and customer base, so with some organisational slack management would likely continue it unless clearer evidence of weak results emerges.
Its dedicated presentation suggests it held a meaningful place in the offer, and as a standard core product it is likely satisfactory enough to stay on the market.

Given its overlap with another tube-heater product and only limited visible prominence, management would be relatively likely to reallocate resources away from it if results fell short of aspiration levels.
